message:
feat(keepalive-multi r1): the table of kept PCs with their resources -- who is on screen, who is parked

SessionTable (session_table.hpp) is the glue the bridge will wrap: the registry, a map of
handle -> entry (shared_ptr, so a call in flight outlives its removal), and the one
decoder's bind/unbind. One transition lock orders reserve / commit / fail / activate /
begin-park / end / end-all / reap; teardowns run through a closer (a detached thread in the
app), never under a table lock, and the entry leaves the registry only after its close.
- BeginPark(A): A's adapter token goes to 0 and the decoder is unbound first, then the
  session's own park (inhibit -> release -> pause -> Pong fence) starts and A's TTL with it.
- Activate(B): refused while another entry is active or still confirming its park; then a
  new binding (process counter), the decoder bound, and a parked B resumed (refused resume
  ends B only).
- End(one) leaves the others; EndAll moves the epoch first; Reap takes off sessions that
  ended on their own (ttl / pause_failed / peer_lost) and a connection never shown (10 s).
The park limit is now a policy value (ClientParkFence::SetParkedLimitUs, controller
SetParkLimitMs) still enforced by each session's own control loop; 5 min by default.
session_table_test 45/0 (x5, race case ~10^5 lookups): A->B fence order, A->B->A->B reuse
with 4 distinct bindings, one end keeps the others with an off-lock teardown, end-all
epoch + late commit refused, LRU at the 4th PC with failures evicting nothing, self-ended
sessions reaped without reconnect, resume refused / no pause / never shown. Negative
control: the registry alone lets B on screen while A's pause is unconfirmed.
client_park_state 34/0, session_registry 31/0.
